Hi maintainers, could you please reopen PR #43890? It was previously closed after hitting a CI issue from using by decide on prime checks, which has now been fixed and refactored.

(Note: I am a non-native English speaker. I wrote this message in Chinese myself and used Google Translate to communicate. This is not generated by an LLM.)

It was closed for a different reason: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/43890#issuecomment-5715647933

There are still unprocessed reviewer comments.

@Johan Commelin Thanks Johan! I actually pushed the commit directly and replied to those review comments in the main PR discussion below, rather than resolving each inline thread.

In the latest commit, I also refactored the approach to use Fermat witnesses (b = 2 and 3), so those old tables are completely removed. I will mark those inline threads as resolved now.
Hey, I was working on a similar PR when yours was closed. You should look at it to find out what was missing from yours: #43965

@Yaël Dillies I think my approach is better and much simpler for closing this TODO: it is just 88 lines of pure Lean using Fermat witnesses (base 2 and 3), without needing a heavy norm_num meta extension.

Once Mathlib has a fast general prime decider in the future, combining it directly with Korselt's criterion will be much cleaner anyway.
But closing the TODO is only part of the story. We also want to make _proving_ that a number is Carmichael easy

Moderation note: I have deleted some AI-generated comments at the end of this thread.
Using AI to write comments is against the rules on this site (#community-guidelines). Please use your own words instead.
